overview.summary: LEO Pharma is the only pure-play dermatology pharma company among Almirall's competitors. Their strategy is anchored on tralokinumab (Adtralza/Adbry), an anti-IL-13 biologic that directly competes with Almirall's Ebglyss (lebrikizumab) in atopic dermatitis. LEO is investing heavily in derm-immunology pipeline expansion (delgocitinib, anti-IL-13 next-gen) while maintaining their legacy topical portfolio (Enstilar, Protopic). As a foundation-owned company, they can take longer-term R&D bets without quarterly earnings pressure.
keyStrengths: Pure derm focus: 100% of R&D and commercial org dedicated to skin diseases
Tralokinumab (Adtralza): first-to-market anti-IL-13 in AD in Europe
Foundation ownership allows long-term derm investment without short-term earnings pressure
Deep dermatology KOL relationships and specialized sales force across Europe
overview.threatRationale: LEO Pharma is Almirall's most direct competitor in mechanism and positioning. Tralokinumab (anti-IL-13) and lebrikizumab (anti-IL-13) share the same target, making this a head-to-head commercial battle in AD. LEO's pure-derm focus, earlier EU launch, and topical portfolio synergies give them commercial leverage in dermatologist offices where Almirall also competes.
